stories.stat_label: kids get a free hot school meal
stories.headline: Ukraine now feeds 3 million kids free hot school meals
stories.summary: Since September, pupils in grades 1-11 at municipal schools get a free hot lunch, about 3 million kids. In frontline Romny, one school cooks 350 meals a day and serves them in shelters during air raids.
stories.why: A hot meal brings kids to school and helps them learn, even in a war.

stories.headline: Ethiopians planted 47 billion tree seedlings in 7 years
stories.summary: Tens of millions of volunteers joined the Green Legacy drive, which aims for 50 billion by 2030. A 2026 study of 44,500 seedlings planted in the south found about 80% had survived.
stories.why: Trees hold soil and water on farms hit by floods and drought.

stories.headline: A giant sea 'woodlouse' in a drawer was a new species
stories.summary: A deep-sea isopod kept in a German university collection since the 1980s turned out to be unknown to science. Named Bathynomus tuebingoborikensis, it honours Tübingen and Puerto Rico's Taíno name.
stories.why: Old museum drawers can still hold brand-new species.

stories.stat_label: the last time anyone recorded it
stories.headline: A frog lost since 1985 was found again in the Himalayas
stories.summary: Searching 14 sites for 424 hours, researchers found just two Chakrata torrent frogs, 65 km from where it was last seen, and read the species' DNA for the first time.
stories.why: A critically endangered frog is still out there, and can now be protected.

fun_fact: Giant isopods are cousins of garden woodlice, and some grow up to 50 cm long.
